name: crowagent-website-astro
//engines: R262-WEB-01. Astro 6 and 7 require Node >= 22.12.0; Astro 5 did not. This repo had NO .nvmrc, .node-version or engines field, and the Cloudflare Pages build settings are dashboard-only, so the first deploy after the Astro 7 upgrade would have failed at `npm ci` on any build image still serving Node 18 or an older 22.x — with an error about a dependency, not about Node. Pages resolves the version from NODE_VERSION, .nvmrc or .node-version (Cloudflare build-image docs), so a `.nvmrc` is committed at BOTH the repo root and `astro/` because the Pages build root is not visible from here and covering both removes the guess. 24.18.0 is the line this was actually verified on: the 33-gate chain went 33/33 on local Node 24.14.0, the Astro 5 control build passed on the same runtime, CI (.github/workflows/astro-gates.yml) uses Node 24, and 24.18.0 is preinstalled in the Cloudflare build image so it costs no download. This field is the declaration; the .nvmrc files are what Pages actually reads.
description: The modernised crowagent.ai. Isolated from the legacy tree on purpose: the live site keeps building and deploying from the repo root until this one is verified route-for-route against tag baseline-transformed-2026-08-01.

scripts.//build: R262-D-72. Was a single `&&` chain of 31 steps: the first failure stopped every gate after it from ever running, which is how check-palette-roles.js and check-render.js went unrun against WorkstationTour.astro on the build that shipped it. scripts/run-gates.mjs declares the same 31 steps in the same order and runs all of them regardless of earlier failures, prints every gate's own output plus one summary naming every pass and fail, and still exits 1 if anything failed.
scripts.//build:deploy: WHAT CLOUDFLARE PAGES RUNS. Produces the artefact and nothing else: four source guards, a type-check, the build, and the three steps that EMIT files (copy-assets, copy-cf-config, build-sitemap). It deliberately omits the ~20 browser-driving gates in `build`, because those are CERTIFICATION and belong on a developer machine. Added 2026-08-05 after the first Astro deploy failed at 35s: npm ci and astro build both succeeded and the chain died where the Playwright gates begin. Re-running certification on every deploy is slow, spends build minutes, and fails for environment reasons that say nothing about the site. Certify with `npm run build` locally BEFORE pushing; this script is not a substitute for it.
scripts.build:deploy: node scripts/check-comment-terminators.js && node scripts/check-facts.js && node scripts/check-english.js && node scripts/check-vendor-logos.js && astro check && astro build && node scripts/copy-assets.js && node scripts/copy-cf-config.js && node scripts/build-sitemap.js
